bug_semantics: A syntactically valid quoted Git config value can contain an escaped \n that GitPython decodes into an embedded LF while reading. Before 3.1.59, GitConfigParser._write()/write_section() re-serialized that resident LF as a bare physical newline followed only by a tab, rather than as a Git-compatible quoted escape/continuation. An attacker-shaped inert value such as A\nhooksPath = ../evil-hooks therefore becomes a separate live core.hooksPath directive after any unrelated GitPython config write, and a later hook-firing Git operation can execute attacker-controlled code.
flaw_origin:
Commit b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e completed the vulnerable mechanism by adding multi-line quote state and string_decode() to git/config.py:247-324; string_decode() used unicode_escape/string_escape, converting a literal 
 sequence into an embedded LF stored in _sections. The already-existing writer at git/config.py:366-373 emitted embedded LFs with replace('
', '
	') and no quoting or backslash continuation. The direct parent had that unsafe serializer but no multi-line state, string_decode(), unicode_escape/string_escape decoding, or corresponding call sites, so it could not create this read-to-rewrite path from the advisory's standard quoted multi-line input.
ai_marker: absent: the exact b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e commit object names Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com> as both author and committer and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, agent marker, or bot identity in its message or trailers.
evidence: The repository's first-party advisory is https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-284h-m62q-gf8w (API record: https://api.github.com/repos/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security-advisories/GHSA-284h-m62q-gf8w). It identifies git/config.py _read()/string_decode() and _write()/write_section(), describes the dormant quoted multi-line value -> unrelated write -> injected core.hooksPath -> hook execution path, and declares affected versions <= 3.1.58 and patched versions >= 3.1.59. The assigned alias advisory is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9557-234j-7rv9 for CVE-2026-78676.

History search in the read-only clone: git log -S'string_decode' --all found b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e as the 2015 introduction (later hits are edits/removal), while git log -L 247,263:git/config.py at that revision showed b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e adding is_multi_line, string_decode(), and unicode_escape/string_escape decoding. Its diff also adds the multi-line detection/calls at git/config.py:307-324. Commit URL: https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/commit/b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e.

Direct-parent verification: b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e^ resolves to a0cb95c5df7a559633c48f5b0f200599c4a62091. A parent-tree git grep for string_decode, is_multi_line, unicode_escape, and string_escape returned no match, and the BIC diff shows those lines as additions. The parent did contain the older unsafe serializer at git/config.py:344, str(value).replace('\n', '\n\t'), proving b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e was the smallest non-move commit that supplied the missing decode/continuation half of the complete vulnerable lifecycle.

Serializer provenance was separately decomposed to exclude moves/refactors: git log -S"replace('\n', '\n\t')" --all traces the original writer to 3fd37230e76a014cf5c45d55daf0be2caa6948b7 (lib/git/config.py), with later path moves/imports and formatting commits. That 2009 commit alone did not parse the advisory's quoted multi-line input into an embedded LF; b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e is the first revision where the old writer and new decoding behavior coexist.

Version boundary check: 0.3.4 peels to b18fd3fd13d0a1de0c3067292796e011f0f01a05 and does not contain the BIC; 0.3.5 peels to a2d39529eea4d0ecfcd65a2d245284174cd2e0aa and 0.3.4..0.3.5 contains b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e, making 0.3.5 the first tagged release with the reconstructed mechanism. The BIC remains in every subsequent release through 3.1.58, consistent with the first-party advisory's coarse <= 3.1.58 range.

Fix evidence: https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/commit/4b4e47fc1224e23b0c8ee7220a7192818f2e4abb replaces the bare-newline writer in git/config.py:705-712 with Git-compatible quoting and escaping of LF/tab/backspace/backslash/quote. Its regression starts from the inert multi-line core.zzz payload, performs an unrelated set_value(), then checks with both GitPython and git config that no core.hooksPath option is created. Tag 3.1.58 peels to 30be45d786e95023e23c616fec5cbabca861b44c and lacks the fix; tag 3.1.59 peels to 66340d77aab9a7468f4aed3681d4ef1e3c0ec931, and git log 3.1.58..3.1.59 contains 4b4e47fc1224e23b0c8ee7220a7192818f2e4abb, matching the patched >= 3.1.59 boundary.

BIC-only AI inspection used git cat-file commit b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e. The one-parent commit object has human author/committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>, a conventional issue-fixing message ending in Fixes #112, and no AI authorship, co-authorship, generation trailer, or bot marker. No later commit or fix attribution was used for the verdict.
reasoning: The first-party advisory makes the vulnerability a two-part read/write round-trip failure, not merely the existence of a permissive writer. The unsafe writer originated in 2009, but until b825dc74773ffa5c7a45b48d72616b222ad2023e GitPython's custom reader lacked the quote-continuation state and escape decoder needed to turn the advisory's valid dormant on-disk value into an in-memory LF. The BIC adds exactly that missing behavior; its direct parent demonstrably lacks the added lines while retaining the writer, so the complete exploit mechanism first exists in the BIC. The BIC is a normal single-parent implementation commit, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate. It enters tag 0.3.5 and persists through 3.1.58. Direct fix 4b4e47fc1224e23b0c8ee7220a7192818f2e4abb makes resident special-character values serialize as quoted Git-compatible escapes and is included in 3.1.59, matching the first-party boundary. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has only human author/committer identity and no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any attribution on later history.
